entries.Don’t be afraid. If any more of these pa: Don’t be afraid. If any more of these pathetic humans come, we’ll deal with them the way we did with this rubbish!
entries.Then move Kapou’e to the signpost in the: Then move Kapou’e to the signpost in the north-east
entries.Move Kapou’e to the signpost in the nort: Move Kapou’e to the signpost in the north-east
entries.Hmmm. $scout.name, go find out what they: Hmmm. $scout.name, go and find out what they are up to.
entries.Well... the humans want to... meet with: Well... the humans want to... meet them.
entries.Hahaha! If you can!: Ha ha ha! If you can!
Fine, someone go and release him.
entries.Since it was now obvious that the humans: Since it was now obvious that the humans were going to try their best to prevent that by capturing or killing the shamans, Kapou’e was requested to escort the shamans to the harbour of Tirigaz where the rest of the Council was residing.
entries.Hmmm, what a neat bottle! What is it?: Hmmm, what a nice bottle! What is it?
entries.Listen, if we are to meet with the rest: Listen, if we are to meet the rest of the Great Council, we have to repel this attack. You shamans hide here in the forest until we defeat them. It will be faster and easier for us if we don’t have to worry about protecting you.
entries.Haha! Our plan is going well, let’s surr: Ha ha! Our plan is going well, let’s surround them on land while our allies attack them from sea!
entries.Look, a party of our kind approaches fro: Look, a party of our kind approaches from the north.
entries.Son of the great Black-Eye Karun?! You d: Son of the great Black-Eye Karun?! You do us honour, Chief.
entries.I don’t really know, one day all was cal: I don’t really know, one day all was calm and peaceful and the next day a fleet of human ships showed up and began spewing out troops. Did our best to hold them off, but they captured the northern keep. And then human reinforcements arrived from their settlements to the south.
entries.Wise decision. We have actually come to: Wise decision. We have actually come to speak to the shamans, but while we are here we must help you out of this scrape. Grüü, fight the humans if you must, but don’t be reckless. Getting me to the Tirigaz keep so I can rally our forces for the counter-attack must be our first priority. And, I need you to stay alive. We can’t defeat them by sea without ships, but we can destroy the foothold they have gained on the land.
entries.We are victorious at last. Someone go te: We are victorious at last. Someone go and tell the shamans that they can come out now.
entries.Congratulations on your victory, Kapou’e: Congratulations on your victory, Kapou’e. You do honour to the memory of your father.
entries.Reach the Oasis in the Southeast: Reach the Oasis in the south-east
entries.I hope we won’t find one! They are terri: I hope we won’t find one! They are terrible armoured beasts; your hammer would be useless against their heavy shells.
entries.Yeah, I can see that. Well, I guess we h: Yeah, I can see that. Well, I suppose we have to clean these rabble out of here.
... Come... on... people...! We have... to... keep... going...
entries.The fact is that few people entered this: The fact is that few people entered this forest and returned home safely. I am not sure, but most likely, this forest is full of elvish renegades.
entries.We made an agreement with the humans som: We made an agreement with the humans some time ago. They were planning a major assault on you warmongers, and the humans pledged that if we assisted them they would give us a large chunk of your territory once the battle was over.
entries.female^With pleasure. But what should I: With pleasure. But what should I do with this weakling?
entries.After clearing out the elves from the Si: After clearing the elves from the Silent Forest, Kapou’e and his party set out on the last leg of their journey. Within a few days they finally reached the city of Lmarig in the Mourned Hills, which was then ruled by Shan Taum the Smug.
entries.Who is that? Kapou’e! What are you doing: Who is that? Kapou’e! What are you doing in my lands you weakling runt?
entries.Bwahaha! You are nothing! Where is your: Bwa ha ha! You are nothing! Where is your land? You became a beggar. You are as pathetic as your father!
entries.Kapou’e, rumors tell of you making a lon: Kapou’e, rumours tell of you making a long trip to seek assistance from us, and escorting Pirk, Gork and Vraurk. The Council is grateful for that.
entries.You don’t understand. Orcs have been div: You don’t understand. Orcs have been divided for ages. The only one who gave us some unity was your father, Black-Eye Karun. When we heard rumours of your exploits, we understood that you are a worthy son of your father.
entries.Go defend Prestim, Kapou’e. In the meant: Go and defend Prestim, Kapou’e. In the meantime, now that the Council is complete again, we will decide. We may have to form the Great Horde again and make you its leader.
entries.So, the elves and dwarves failed to take: So, the elves and dwarves failed to take the fortress and the beasts were able to muster a defence. No matter. Once the vanguard of my army arrives, I will storm their pitiful fortress myself.
entries.Fool! We can hold that long. But we have: Fool! We can hold that long. But we must have Prestim firmly in control when the shamans arrive with the Great Horde. We can’t let the humans establish a foothold on this side of the river...
entries.... because if we cannot decisively beat: ... because if we cannot decisively beat these humans, the other tribes won’t think us strong enough to lead them. Each chieftain will try to claim leadership of the horde for themselves, and the humans will be able to break through our defences.
entries.We arrive to honor our alliance, Earl La: We arrive to honour our alliance, Earl Lanbec’h.
entries.Your defense of Prestim was heroic, faci: Your defence of Prestim was heroic, facing such opposition surely undermined the morale of the humans. Now they are retreating to their fortresses and will not venture out again any time soon.
entries.The horde was then split into two forces: The horde was then split into two forces. On the advice of the shamans, Kapou’e placed one force under the leadership of Shan Taum the Smug, who — despite his obnoxious nature — was a fierce and capable leader. He was sent to Bitok, the most south-western orcish city, to cut off the humans already invading the port city of Tirigaz, and to stop any further human incursion into orcish territory.
entries.Kapou’e himself — desiring to settle thi: Kapou’e himself — desiring to settle this business once and for all — led his remaining forces to Dorest, the human city due south-east of Prestim, to which Earl Lanbec’h had retreated.
entries.Sorry there, old chap. You’re deemed too: Sorry, old chap. You’re deemed too insignificant for the likes of the Earl to deal with. He’s left that pleasure to me instead.
entries.Having broken the dwarvish blockade, the: Having broken the dwarvish blockade, the horde continued through the mountain pass. Kapou’e began to recognize the lands about them and sure enough, they soon found themselves back in the tribe’s homeland.
entries.My men know the land well. Flar’Tar and: My men know the land well. Flar’Tar and Al’Brock, both of you take a scout and circle around to the north-east and south-east respectively. Grüü, you take your trolls and circle around to the north-west. If all goes well, we shall surround them.
entries.Better late than never. Now it’s time to: Better late than never. Now it’s time to kill! Let no-one escape! Everyone, keep an eye out for the shamans.
We had better go and look.
You had better go and look.
entries.Then move Kapou’e to the signpost in the: Then move Kapou’e to the signpost in the south-west
entries.Move Kapou’e to the signpost in the sout: Move Kapou’e to the signpost in the south-west
entries.Furthermore, the troops who had been led: Furthermore, the troops who had been led by Kapou’e this far had grown to respect him as a wise and capable leader, and they proclaimed their loyalty to him. Delighted, Kapou’e sent detachments off in different directions to bring in the other tribes, by force if necessary. Al’Brock was sent west, along the route that Kapou’e had used to flee the human forces almost a year before. Flar’Tar was sent directly south to rally the tribes along the Mountains of Haag and the eastern Mourned Hills. Kapou’e himself made a direct south-west beeline towards Bitok. They were all to meet in Dorest that spring to repel the human attack that seemed certain to come.
entries.It’s been a chilly winter. How about we: It’s been a chilly winter. How about we warm ourselves up a bit by giving these traitors a good beating, boys?
This rabble won’t be a problem any more.
Hee hee, we wiped them out good.
entries.Kapou’e and his followers made a gruelin: Kapou’e and his followers made a gruelling march across the frozen Northlands. For the orcs, it was a constant nightmare of freezing, marching and fighting. Food was scarce, and the stores that they managed to seize from rebellious tribes had to be strictly rationed. Many of the weaker orcs who weren’t killed in combat died from exhaustion or fell behind and froze to death.
Their presence proved to be unnecessary. It came as a shock to Kapou’e to discover, after a few days, that his people held him in awe. News of Kapou’e’s exploits had been widely circulated — from his rescue of the shamans at Barag Gór, to his forced march through the northern blizzards. Younger grunts especially worshipped him with such fervour that he found it almost frightening.
entries.Days passed, the snows melted, and Kapou: Days passed, the snows melted, and Kapou’e readied his defences. A few weeks after Kapou’e’s arrival, riders caught sight of Earl Lanbec’h’s army.
entries.The hell I don’t, Earl Lanbec’h, the Nor: The hell I don’t, Earl Lanbec’h, the Northern Alliance was witness to a treaty some seventeen years ago between your people and the orcs, which both of you are no doubt violating. It is our duty as the orchestrator and witness of this treaty to see that it is honoured.
entries.That having been settled, Kapou’e began: That having been settled, Kapou’e began to enquire about the death of his father. Howgarth III repeated his story, that the last thing they heard from Black-Eye Karun was the message declining their invitation to join the Northern Alliance, brought by none other than Shan Taum himself.
entries.In order to keep fighting between the tr: In order to keep fighting between the tribes to a minimum, Kapou’e also maintained an enormous army, drawn from all corners of his empire. To offset the cost of maintaining such an army, he often hired out portions of it to act as mercenaries in foreign struggles. People of all races took advantage of this and, consequently, those orcs thirsting for battle got more than enough to keep them from attacking their nearest neighbours.
entries.Congratulations, your $unit.language_nam: Congratulations, your $unit.language_name has advanced... but they’re already at their maximum level! When this happens, some campaigns — like this one — allow you to select a minor bonus to hit-points or damage. These bonuses are called ‘AMLAs’: ‘After Maximum Level Advancements’. If your max-level units have normal, blue experience bars, that means these AMLAs are available. Other campaigns don’t have these AMLA options, and instead always give max-level units +3 max HP when they advance. If your max-level units have purple experience bars, they’ll only get +3 max HP when they advance.
